a.text: Dad, why's there a knife on the wall?
That was my constant companion when I was young and begging for food.
So why's there an empty shelf under it?
That's reserved for an old elder of mine.

steps.text: It's early in the morning, and the weather's cloudy.
Along Yingfeng Road in Shangshu of Great Yan, sits an inn.
Not many establishments would call themselves an inn in modern Yan.
But this one has the most antique atmosphere, the finest wine and tea, and is the most cultured in all Shangshu.
Its sign is red with gold lettering.
'Xingyu.'

steps.name: Someone Innkeeper-esque
steps.text: Ten jars of Husong, three jars of Yunliao, six jars of Guixing reserve... hmm...

steps.name: Someone Innkeeper-esque
steps.text: Liu, why are our numbers here so much lower than across the river?

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Don't blame me! They went crazy with banquets at the start of the month. Of course they sold more than us!

steps.name: Someone Innkeeper-esque
steps.text: How much difference can a few parties make?

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Aiyo wei! You don't even know the half of it.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: You were out of Shangshu then. You don't know how ridiculous that hoo-hah was... Those two days of business could pay half a year's worth of bills, no exaggeration.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: We were beating them for months, and those two days completely sunk us. You can't keep letting them make a fool of us, Mr. Zheng.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Remember, we were here first, and were the first to do it well. If you ask me the other places should be bowing to my old man here.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Don't be fooled into loving your grandkids while you forget your son here.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: What are you even blubbering about? Since when am I your old man? I haven't even said anything.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Yeah, and it'll be all over for me once you do.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: It was just bad luck. If I were the one to meet those nobles...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: If it's just bad luck, then where's all your good luck to balance it out?

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Gah! Nobles, nobles, where did all those nobles come from...?

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: We've always relied on word of mouth from our regulars, and you won't even do ads. If we could just invite a few pretty boys and girls to...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: (Glare) ...

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: You heard nothing. That was the wind just now.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Running a restaurant-inn depends on customers with taste and connections, true. But what do you know about who's connected and who isn't?

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: If I knew, I'd be running the inn.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Then sit tight and learn.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Anyone with eyes can discern if someone rich, powerful, stylish, and wise, that's plain as day. So why can't you?

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Erk...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Whether you're a kung fu adventurer or a settled person, so long as you're alive you'll mingle with plenty of other people.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: So keep mingling, and you'll get a good eye for this. Knowing people, and knowing what they know, is what lets us live well.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Meanwhile, you spend all day fiddling about, and run off to the mahjong parlors every night. What kind of future do you expect when...

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Why'd you stop the lecture?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Don't you see our two guests at the door?! Why aren't you greeting them?!

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Aiyo... I completely missed them! Quick, quick, get them in! The first two customers of the day! Get them two plates of salted peanuts and a pot of chrysanthemum tea!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Might our luck be looking up?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: We are early. Let me treat you to dinner in Mr. Liang's stead.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: Take a seat! Tea will be with you in a moment!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I thought we'd have made a beeline for his residence.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Your 'friend' there is still a magistrate. Busy, in any case.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Busy enough to overlook a friend? Must be busy as can be.

steps.name: Inn Assistant
steps.text: (Sir, sir, what do you think, then? Are these two noble-types?)

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Pah.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Don't ask, observe. You can't judge at first glance.

a.text: Shangshu, where the winds blow high, and the clouds part to show off the moon.
The land was mountainous since times untold. Some would say the rugged terrain posed quite the obstacle to the nomadic city's development.
But the folk of Shangshu were loath to give up the land they'd dwelt in since antiquity, so they went to great pains to move mountains and fuse their city with the peaks.
Hence, unlike other cities, Shangshu's plates were distributed along the lines of the range, each perhaps hundreds or thousands of meters wide and utterly unique in their scenery.

How auspicious Shangshu's habitation must be that in recent years it has never once been struck by Catastrophe. Its people have built new towns in the mountains, and opened them up with ropeways and tunnels.
Furthermore, with the guidance of the Tumu Tianshi, a mountain range of particular renown was directly relocated onto the nomadic platforms, where...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Slow down mate, what's a Tumu... Tianshi? 'Heavenly Master of Earth and Wood'?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: You might be unaware, benefactor, but Yan has multiple bureaus of tianshi, Celestial Masters. Any student of the land even a mite accomplished at Originium Arts may apply to join, take layer upon layer of examination, and so serve the country.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Originium Arts have a dizzying array of applications, and the science of Originium is developing by the day. The tianshi of Yan are naturally classified by profession and specialty—civil engineers, for example! The artists of earth and wood indeed.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: And here I thought cool titles like that would be reserved for Casters like Leizi—y'know, ones with crazy battle prowess.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Would Leizi be that Yan official in Rhodes Island you mentioned before? My my, it may have been like that in the past, but times have changed. Now the welfare of the people comes first.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Originium technology benefits the masses, and every tianshi of Yan's Ministry of Works pours their life's blood into researching Originium's Arts and testing new materials.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Other countries couldn't dream of moving whole mountains onto nomadic cities, that's for sure...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Indeed. While landscapes may soothe the soul, it certainly wouldn't be worth such monumental efforts if it broke the backs and the banks of the people in the process.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Still, most of the credit belongs to the civil engineers of the tianshi who loved their home enough to put in the work. And moving mountains was easy compared to convincing the local villages and estates to agree to the project.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Yan has an old proverb. It's a land that raises its people.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: A shame I can't speak much on Originium Arts, or else I'd have the same things on my mind as one of those nomadic city architects.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Is everyone from Yan like this?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: It's these rivers and hills before us, see—

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: The limitless sights. Early springs so tranquil you can hear the snowflakes land. There's a lasting charm about it.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: If you'd lived here since the cradle too, perhaps you'd think the same way.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Maybe. Who can say?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Phew—now that's refreshing.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: 'Where the winds blow high, and the clouds part to show off the moon.' I can see how it earned that.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Within Shangshu lie the renowned 'Three Mounts and Seventeen Peaks,' and they draw plenty of tourists. Some foreign nobility even make the trip out here simply to admire them.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Presumably the common folk owe it only to the pains of crossing the land that these landmarks aren't swarmed by such visitors coming in droves.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: There's a comfy breeze up here. I was worried it'd rain and delay us from heading up the mountains today.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Quite right, benefactor. The spring breeze caresses one's cheeks, the drizzle falls finely, all silent and slick in the rain.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Been meaning to ask, actually. You're a martial artist, right? So how'd you get so... bookish?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: My master often instructed us that practicing the martial arts hardly precludes the study of culture. Indeed, the arts come both martial and cultural. To learn them well is but the duty of the modern soul.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Besides, the art of gab can be a gateway to making some money.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor, what say we visit the nearest summit on the way? I hear more people have taken to the mountains these last two years; there's been quite the hubbub.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Pass. We'll rest in the city for a day or two, wait for the sisters to meet up with us, and head on our way...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: *Sigh* Never felt so bad about missing all the scenery on the way though.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: You've always been singularly devoted, benefactor. A mind only for the objective, not a whit more. And as proof of your conscientiousness, you never take a break.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Never take breaks? Me?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: But of course!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Whatever, flattery will get you nowhere. We're not going.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Er, but you're merely taking me to the office for onboarding. Such a minor errand needn't be so urgent.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: And did I not hear Lava mention you undertook this journey intending a vacation? Surely nothing impedes you from a good tour of the scenery then?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: If only Lava were here... I'm not the only one who needs to sort out her head right now.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactor Lava just happened to be tasked with a sudden commission taking her a different way—I imagine she'll pass by scenery just as fine.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I don't think she's the type to gawp at the view. Not in a million years.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Haha, so she isn't.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: To be honest though, she wasn't always this way. Me neither, of course.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: You needn't brood, benefactor. Things change, we change. The world's affairs are inconstant.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Let's hurry on our way, then.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: Found them, Miss Du.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: You sure?

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: No mistake. They came in at Zhengshan Crossing, and got to Yingfeng Road in Weichang District. He got someone reliable to come with him the whole way.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: And the Lungmenite's carrying an antique little box on him, correct?

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: Yep. Clear as day.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: If anything goes wrong, you're responsible.

steps.name: Street Youth
steps.text: You left this to us. We won't let it go wrong.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Good!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Then we're paying this buccaneer a visit in place of those yellow-bellied oldies!
